_comment: CORRECTED. The committed template could not deploy. Changes:
1. BLOCKER - every rule was missing the required 'scopes' property.
scheduledQueryRules 2023-03-15 rejects the template without it.
2. BLOCKER - all four rules referenced actionGroups 'ag-soc-<env>',
which no template, and neither main.tf nor infra/, ever created.
The action group is now created here as resource[0] and everything
else dependsOn it. The actionGroupEmail parameter, previously
declared and never used, now feeds it.
3. BUG - alert 2 queried the Application Insights 'customMetrics'
table. APIM emit-metric writes to Azure Monitor CUSTOM METRICS, a
different store that is not queryable from Log Analytics KQL. The
alert could never fire. Converted to a metricAlert against the
SOC-AI/ai_call_count metric namespace, which is where the data is.
4. SEMANTICS - alert 3 fired on HTTP 400 from the PHI check-header
policy. That is the control WORKING, not a bypass. Paging at
severity 0 because a client forgot a header is alert fatigue, and
the real failure mode - PHI reaching the model WITH the header set
true - was invisible. Now split into two rules: a sev-2 on blocked
traffic (misconfigured client), and a sev-0 on sanitizer failure
emitted by the application itself, which is the only place a true
bypass is observable.
5. MISMATCH - alert 4 queried KubeNodeInventory for 'aks-wazuh'.
infra/ deploys Wazuh on a VM; only main.tf creates AKS. Now
parameterised by wazuhComputeMode so one template serves both.
6. Added metricMeasureColumn on the rules whose queries summarize into
a named column while declaring a non-Count aggregation. Without it
ARM rejects the criteria.
7. Added autoMitigate so resolved conditions clear themselves.

metadata.description: Email address for all SOC cost and compliance alerts
Full resource ID of the Log Analytics workspace. Required scope for every scheduled query rule.
Full resource ID of the APIM instance. Scope for the ai_call_count metric alert.

wazuhOfflineQuery.vm: Heartbeat | where Computer startswith 'vm-wazuh' | summarize LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer | where LastSeen < ago(10m)
wazuhOfflineQuery.aks: KubeNodeInventory | where ClusterName contains 'aks-wazuh' | where Status == 'Ready' | summarize NodeCount = dcount(Computer) by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m) | where NodeCount < 2

resources.comments: Action group. Previously referenced by all four rules and never created.
resources.name: [variables('actionGroupName')]

resources.comments: Alert 1: GPU spot cluster active outside the 00:00-06:00 UTC training window. NOTE: this definition pages on any legitimate daytime training run. If you train ad hoc, gate on cumulative node-hours per day instead of wall-clock hour.
resources.name: [concat('alert-gpu-runaway-', parameters('env'))]

properties.displayName: GPU spot cluster active outside training window

allOf.query: AmlComputeClusterEvent | where ClusterName contains 'gpu-spot' | where TargetNodeCount > 0 | where datetime_part('Hour', TimeGenerated) !between (0 .. 6)

resources.comments: Alert 2: AI call volume spike. Converted from a scheduledQueryRule over customMetrics (wrong store - the data is never there) to a metricAlert over the SOC-AI custom metric namespace that APIM emit-metric actually writes to.
resources.name: [concat('alert-apim-call-spike-', parameters('env'))]

properties.description: APIM AI call volume exceeded 500k/hour - likely a runaway client loop or prompt-injection retry storm.

resources.comments: Alert 3a: the PHI header check is REJECTING traffic. This is the control working correctly against a misconfigured client - severity 2, not 0. The committed template paged at severity 0 for this.
resources.name: [concat('alert-phi-header-rejects-', parameters('env'))]

properties.displayName: PHI sanitization header check is rejecting requests
properties.description: A caller is reaching the AI gateway without X-PHI-Sanitized. The control is holding, but a client is misconfigured and its alerts are not being triaged.

allOf.query: ApiManagementGatewayLogs | where ResponseCode == 400 | where LastErrorMessage has 'PHI-sanitized'

resources.comments: Alert 3b: THE REAL SEVERITY-0. A genuine PHI bypass is unsanitized content reaching the model, which the gateway cannot see because the header is caller-asserted. It is only observable where sanitization runs. This queries the phi.sanitize_failed event emitted by src/common/phi.py (see patches/src_common_phi.py). Until that module is wired in, this rule has no data source - which is itself the finding.
resources.name: [concat('alert-phi-bypass-', parameters('env'))]

properties.displayName: HIPAA CRITICAL - PHI sanitization failed open
properties.description: The sanitizer failed and an alert may have reached the model unsanitized. Investigate immediately and quarantine the affected model inputs.

allOf.query: AppTraces | where Message has 'phi.sanitize_failed' or Message has 'phi.attestation_missing' | project TimeGenerated, Message, AppRoleName

resources.comments: Alert 4: Wazuh compute offline. Query switches on wazuhComputeMode because infra/ deploys a VM and main.tf deploys AKS - the committed template only handled AKS, which infra/ never creates.
resources.name: [concat('alert-wazuh-offline-', parameters('env'))]

properties.displayName: Wazuh SIEM offline or below minimum capacity
properties.description: The SIEM is not reporting. Alert ingestion has stopped; the AI tiers have nothing to triage and the gap will not be visible anywhere else.
